unit.label: Holidays, plans & feasibility
unit.title: What Are You Planning?
unit.description: 11 genuinely new these lessons words and forms. Close the this lesson tail, then talk about breaks, travel plans, and when something will happen.

goal.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn gēn péngyǒu qù lǚxíng.
goal.meaning: I plan to travel with friends.

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 8 Vocabulary II tail (printed pp. 164–165) and Lesson 9 Dialogue I / Vocabulary I plus the Time-When side of Grammar I (printed pp. 183–188). 古代 and 不行 close the explicit Unit 25 deferral; time-duration structure continues in Unit 27.

lessons.title: Ancient Things — and a Plan That Won’t Work
lessons.subtitle: Close the two this lesson items intentionally left after Unit 25.

steps.prompt: A proposed route is impossible because there is no MRT there. Which response fits?
steps.explanation: 不行 rejects the plan as not workable.

steps.prompt: Listen to the word and choose its final character.
steps.explanation: In 不行, 行 is pronounced xíng.

lessons.title: Next Week Is a Break
lessons.subtitle: Build 星期 and 放假, then combine them with familiar time words.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says we have a break next week?
steps.explanation: 放假 means have a break. Both 下個星期我們放假 and 我們下個星期放假 are valid time placements.

steps.prompt: Which word means “to have a holiday / be on break”?
steps.explanation: 放假 means to have a holiday or a break from the normal schedule.

steps.prompt: 星期六 means which day?
steps.explanation: 星期 + 六 gives Saturday because 六 is six.

lessons.title: Return Home or Go Out
lessons.subtitle: Use 回國 for returning to your country and 出去 for going out.

steps.prompt: You are leaving your current place to have fun. Which verb fits?
steps.explanation: 出去 means to go out; 回國 specifically means return to one's country.

steps.prompt: Which expression specifically means “return to one’s country”?
steps.explanation: 回國 combines 回 “return” with 國 “country.”

lessons.title: Make a Travel Plan
lessons.subtitle: Use 打算 before the action you intend to do.

steps.prompt: Which sentence explicitly presents a plan or intention?
steps.explanation: 打算 introduces the planned action.

steps.prompt: Which word means “to travel / take a trip”?
steps.explanation: 旅行 is the verb for travel here.

lessons.title: A Quiet Plan at Home
lessons.subtitle: Talk about TV and homework without adding new grammar.

steps.prompt: Which word means “homework”?
steps.explanation: 功課 is homework.

steps.prompt: Which expression means “watch TV”?
steps.explanation: 電視 is television, so 看電視 means watch TV.

lessons.title: When Does the Plan Happen?
lessons.subtitle: Separate “when” from the duration pattern that comes next.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says I want to go out on Saturday?
steps.explanation: 星期六 is Saturday; 出去玩 means go out and have fun. The time can also follow 我.

steps.prompt: Which expression answers “when?” rather than “how long?”
steps.explanation: 下個星期 identifies when the event happens.

steps.prompt: In 我大概下個星期回國, what does 大概 mean?
steps.explanation: 大概 can express an approximate judgment or probability; here it means probably.

steps.explanation: In 不行, 行 is xíng.

steps.explanation: 假 has 亻 on the left and 叚 on the right.

steps.explanation: 古代 refers to ancient times or something ancient.

steps.prompt: Your proposed route cannot work. Which response directly rejects its feasibility?
steps.explanation: 不行 means the proposed plan will not work.

steps.prompt: Which sentence says we have a break next week?
steps.explanation: 放假 means have a break. Both 下個星期我們放假 and 我們下個星期放假 are valid time placements.

steps.prompt: Which order places the time-when expression before the action?
steps.explanation: 下個星期 comes before the main action 回國.

steps.prompt: Which word means “go out” rather than “return to one’s country”?

newVocabulary.note: Here 不行 rejects a proposed plan because it is not feasible.

newVocabulary.meaning: to have a holiday; be on break

古.note: 古 is gǔ in 古代, meaning ancient times or something ancient.
古.memory: 十 sits above 口. Keep the top cross centered over the box.

parts.label: 十
parts.name: top cross
parts.description: The first two strokes form 十 above the lower box.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: lower box
parts.description: The last three strokes form 口 beneath the cross.

代.note: 代 is fourth-tone dài. In 古代 it completes the word for ancient times.
代.memory: 亻 is narrow on the left; 弋 opens to the right with a final dot.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form the narrow 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 弋
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The final three strokes form 弋 on the right.

行.note: Read 行 as xíng in 不行 bùxíng, meaning that a proposal will not work. 行 is polyphonic; another reading is háng in words such as 銀行.
行.memory: 彳 gives three stepping strokes on the left; 亍 supplies the two horizontals and vertical hook on the right.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: left step component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 彳 on the left.

parts.label: 亍
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last three strokes form 亍 on the right.

星.meaning: star; first character of 星期
星.note: 星 is first-tone xīng. Learn it here as the first character of 星期, week.
星.memory: 日 sits above 生. Keep the lower 生 centered and slightly wider.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 日 at the top.

parts.label: 生
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The last five strokes form 生 below.

期.note: 期 is second-tone qí in 星期. It refers to a period or scheduled span of time.
期.memory: 其 fills the left side and 月 the right; keep 月 tall and narrow.

parts.label: 其
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first eight strokes form 其 on the left.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The last four strokes form 月 on the right.

放.meaning: release; put; first character of 放假
放.note: 放 is fourth-tone fàng. In 放假 it means to be released from normal work or class for a break.
放.memory: 方 is on the left; 攵 on the right ends with the long falling stroke.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 方 on the left.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: action component
parts.description: The final four strokes form 攵 on the right.

假.note: Read 假 as jià in 放假, where it means a holiday or leave from work or class.
假.memory: 亻 is the two-stroke left side; the larger 叚 component fills the right.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: The first two strokes form 亻 on the left.

parts.label: 叚
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The remaining nine strokes form 叚 on the right.

回.note: 回 is second-tone huí. In 回國 it means return to one's country.
回.memory: The outer 囗 surrounds a smaller 口. The outside closes only after the inner box is finished.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: The outer enclosure uses the first two strokes and the final closing stroke; this visual group is interrupted by the inner 口.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: inner box
parts.description: The middle three strokes form the inner 口.

國.note: 國 is the Traditional character for country. Learn it in 回國.
國.memory: The outer 囗 encloses 或; write the closing bottom stroke of 囗 last.

parts.label: 囗
parts.name: outer enclosure
parts.description: The enclosure begins with two strokes and closes with the final stroke after the inside is complete.

parts.label: 或
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: The eight middle strokes form 或 inside the enclosure.

出.note: 出 is first-tone chū. 出去 combines 出 with the familiar 去 to mean go out.
出.memory: The central vertical runs through an upper open bowl and a lower bowl. Write the central stroke first, then the upper bowl, then the lower bowl; the two visual groups interleave.

parts.label: 山-shape
parts.name: linked mountain strokes
parts.description: The first, fourth, and fifth strokes complete the 山-like linked shape.

parts.label: 凵
parts.name: lower open box
parts.description: The second and third strokes form the upper open 凵; the central vertical and lower bowl form the other visual group.

算.note: 算 is fourth-tone suàn. In 打算, the whole word means to plan or intend to do something.
算.memory: The six-stroke bamboo top 𥫗 sits over the eight-stroke lower block 𥃲.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The first six strokes form the paired bamboo marks at the top.

parts.label: 𥃲
parts.name: lower component
parts.description: The remaining eight strokes form the lower component.

旅.note: 旅 is third-tone lǚ. In 旅行 it names travel or a trip.
旅.memory: 方 begins the left side; two short middle strokes lead into the four-stroke lower-right 𧘇 shape.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: left component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 方.

parts.label: 𠂉
parts.name: upper-right strokes
parts.description: The next two strokes form the small upper-right group.

parts.label: 𧘇
parts.name: lower-right group
parts.description: The final four strokes spread through the lower-right portion.

視.note: 視 is fourth-tone shì. In 電視 it is the second character of the word for television.
視.memory: 礻 is the narrow four-stroke left side; 見 is the seven-stroke right side.

parts.label: 礻
parts.name: spirit component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 礻 on the left.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: seeing component
parts.description: The last seven strokes form 見 on the right.

功.note: 功 is first-tone gōng. In 功課, the whole word means homework.
功.memory: 工 forms the left three strokes and 力 forms the two-stroke right side.

parts.label: 工
parts.name: work component
parts.description: The first three strokes form 工 on the left.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: The final two strokes form 力 on the right.

概.note: 概 is fourth-tone gài. In 大概, the whole word means approximately or probably.
概.memory: 木 is narrow on the left; 既 fills the larger right side.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood component
parts.description: The first four strokes form 木 on the left.

parts.label: 既
parts.name: right component
parts.description: The remaining nine strokes form 既 on the right.

u26-buxing-feasibility.title: Reject an unworkable plan with 不行
u26-buxing-feasibility.explanation: 不行 is a fixed, common response meaning that a proposal will not work or is not feasible. In this situation, taking the MRT is rejected because there is no MRT to the destination. Do not read this use as a simple word-for-word combination of 不 plus every possible meaning of 行.

examples.meaning: That won't work; there is no MRT here.

u26-buxing-feasibility.remember: Use 不行 to reject feasibility or acceptability; give the reason separately when useful.

u26-dasuan-plan.title: State a plan with 打算
u26-dasuan-plan.explanation: 打算 introduces an intention or plan. Put the action being planned directly after 打算. It is more explicitly about a plan than simply saying 想, which often expresses what someone wants to do. To say you do not plan to do it, put 不 before 打算. Ask about a plan with 打算 + action + 嗎, or ask what is planned with 打算做什麼. A negative plan is not the same as being unable to do the action.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn gēn péngyǒu qù lǚxíng.
examples.meaning: I plan to travel with friends.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn zài jiā kàn diànshì.
examples.meaning: I plan to watch TV at home.
I do not plan to return to my country.
Do you plan to return to your country?

u26-dasuan-plan.remember: 打算 + action = plan/intend to do that action.

u26-time-when.title: Put a time-when expression before the action
u26-time-when.pattern: Subject + Time-When + Verb Phrase / Time-When + Subject + Verb Phrase
u26-time-when.explanation: this lesson distinguishes when something happens from how long it lasts. A time-when expression such as 下個星期 identifies the point or period when the event occurs and appears before the main action. It can follow the subject or be moved to the front as the topic.

examples.meaning: I will return to my country next week.
We have a break next week.

u26-time-when.remember: When? goes before the action. How long? is a different pattern, taught next.

u26-ancient-things.note: 古代 modifies 東西 through 的.

u26-buxing.meaning: That won't work; there is no MRT here.
u26-buxing.note: 不行 rejects the proposal as infeasible; the second clause gives the reason.

u26-break-next-week.meaning: We have a break next week.
u26-break-next-week.note: 星期 means week. 下個星期 means next week. Weekdays use 星期 + a number: 星期一 is Monday through 星期六, Saturday; Sunday is 星期日 or 星期天. 放假 means have a holiday or break.

u26-return-next-week.meaning: I will return to my country next week.
u26-return-next-week.note: The time expression comes before the main action 回國.

u26-go-out.meaning: I want to go out and have fun.
u26-go-out.note: 出去 means to go out, away from the current place.

u26-plan-travel.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn gēn péngyǒu qù lǚxíng.
u26-plan-travel.meaning: I plan to travel with friends.
u26-plan-travel.note: 打算 introduces the planned action; 跟朋友 marks the companions.

u26-plan-tv.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn zài jiā kàn diànshì.
u26-plan-tv.meaning: I plan to watch TV at home.
u26-plan-tv.note: 在家 gives the location before the action 看電視.

u26-probably-return.pinyin: Wǒ dàgài xià ge xīngqí huíguó.
u26-probably-return.meaning: I will probably return to my country next week.
u26-probably-return.note: 大概 here expresses probability: probably.

u26-saturday-out.meaning: On Saturday I want to go out and have fun.
u26-saturday-out.note: 星期六 is a time-when expression placed before the action.
